No REPAIRED line is persisted anywhere under grocery/ (grep of *.log, *.txt, *.jsonl), so the item's 1 occurrence cannot be independently recounted
items.root_cause: The hooks git runs for EVERY checkout are copies in the common .git/hooks, refreshed only by an explicit ops/install-hooks.ps1 or by the 10:30 watchdog's daily -Repair. None of the three roads that move the main checkout's HEAD to a landed tip (the bots' lib/checkout-sync.ps1, the scheduled tasks' grocery/sync-production-checkout.ps1, push-main's reset --keep) reinstalls, so the main checkout and every worktree run the previous hook for hours after an ops/hooks change lands: 26 of the last 27 such landings, modeled median 18 h.

root_fix.what: One helper, Update-TcInstalledHooks, called by each of the three HEAD movers right after a successful move. It reinstalls only when the moved range changed a top-level ops/hooks file, never throws, and never changes its caller's outcome; the watchdog's daily -Repair stays as the backstop.
files: lib/checkout-sync.ps1: Invoke-TcCheckoutSync, after the update-ref that moved refs/heads/main (the ~1070/1076 swap and the ~828 interrupted-move finish), with H0 and the new tip
grocery/sync-production-checkout.ps1: record HEAD before the pull; after a pull that exited 0 and moved HEAD, call the helper
ops/push-main.ps1: $landedSync, after the 'reset-keep' branch succeeds (never on 'manual'), against $vwMainDir with $vwStartHead..$landed
lib/test-checkout-sync.ps1, the ops/push-main selftest case files, grocery/sync-production-checkout.ps1 -SelfTest block
root_fix.exact_change: Update-TcInstalledHooks: run 'git -C <Repo> diff --name-only <From> <To> -- ops/hooks' under Clear-TcGitRepoEnv; keep only paths with no further slash below ops/hooks/ (the files install-hooks copies). If none: return @{ ran=$false }. Else invoke ops/install-hooks.ps1 (plain install and verify, which already writes through Write-TcAtomicFile) through Invoke-NativeScript (og-04), print one line 'hook-refresh: reinstalled <files> (install-hooks exit N)', and return @{ ran=$true; rc=N; files=... }. A non-zero rc prints 'hook-refresh: install exited N; the 10:30 watchdog -Repair will retry' and returns; it never throws and never alters the caller's exit or outcome. It takes no lock and makes no blocking wait, so running inside checkout-sync's capture-run mutex (lock order 0) nests nothing (og-27). In push-main, prefer calling it after the push lock is released; if $landedSync runs inside the lock it is still a sub-second copy with no wait, but say which in the commit. ALTERNATIVES REJECTED: (1) installed hook as a shim that execs the tree file: it would arm whatever sits uncommitted in the main checkout for every worktree's commit and push, the main tree itself lags origin until a sync so the lag only moves, and install-hooks' verify-by-bytes plus audit-hook-installed would both need redesign; (2) core.hooksPath=ops/hooks: each worktree then runs its own tree's hooks, so a worktree that edits pre-push weakens its own gate; (3) a git post-merge or post-rewrite hook: reset and update-ref fire neither.

open_questions_for_brad.question: Each grocery item has a price ceiling worked out from real prices. Items above it stay off the board. Today that blocks 1,284 products. For 1,262 of them it changes nothing a shopper sees, because the same store already shows a cheaper one, or the row has since dropped out. Only 22 matter: a real product at a store that has nothing else in that aisle, such as Head and Shoulders at Aldi or freeze-dried basil at Family Fare. Should those 22 stay off?
options: A: keep the ceiling. Those 22 stores show no price for that item, and a wrong product priced above the ceiling (like candy on peanut butter) also stays off.
B: let full-priced real rows through above the ceiling. The 22 stores gain a price, but every wrong product above the ceiling then needs its own exclusion first. That is weeks of matching work.
C: keep the ceiling but list those rows for review instead of silently blocking them. Same result as A on the board, plus a review list.
open_questions_for_brad.recommendation: A. The board's job is the cheapest real price per store, and a premium brand at a store with nothing cheaper almost never changes where a shopper should go. B trades a quiet protection for weeks of exclusion work.
open_questions_for_brad.consequence_of_no_answer: Nothing on the board moves. 0c812e stays open as a record, and the 22 gaps stay gaps.
